The <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>hero of awakening</gloss> <term>Mahasattva</term> <gloss>great being</gloss> also brings the six <term>paramitas</term> <gloss>perfections</gloss> to complete fulfillment. He also draws near to the state of <term>sarvakara-jnana</term> <gloss>omniscience in all aspects</gloss>. Furthermore, Subhuti, when a Bodhisattva Mahasattva practices the six perfections, if he sees sentient beings born in the four ways—born from an egg, born from a womb, born from heat and moisture, or born miraculously—he should investigate in this way: "In the Buddha-field where I shall manifest complete and perfect awakening in unsurpassed, true, and complete enlightenment, may these three states of being born from an egg, born from a womb, and born from heat and moisture not occur and not exist. Instead, may all sentient beings be born miraculously." He should practice the six perfections in such a way. He should completely purify the Buddha-field. He should bring sentient beings to full maturity. Subhuti, a Bodhisattva Mahasattva who practices in that way brings the six perfections to complete fulfillment. He also draws near to the state of omniscience in all aspects. <summary>This page describes the Bodhisattva's vow to purify their future Buddha-field by ensuring all inhabitants are born miraculously rather than through lower forms of birth. It emphasizes that such aspirations bring the practitioner closer to total omniscience.</summary>
